resources.string: Keeps the webhook receiver running so voice notes are not lost.
Tells you when a voice note did not go where it should have.
No access to “%1$s”. Add that folder to this app’s Storage Scopes, then the note can be filed.\n\n“%2$s”
No length found in “%1$s”. Try “timer for ten minutes”.
Tap to add a calendar event
There was no note for today, so one was created at %1$s.
The vault config could not be read (%1$s), so the built-in defaults are in use.
Receiver stopped — voice notes will be lost
No webhook secret — every request is rejected
Timers and calendar events fire directly
Timers and calendar events need a notification tap — grant “Display over other apps” to fire them directly
Where should the app keep its files?

One folder inside the vault holds everything this app writes: tasks, notes, recordings, its config and the maps. Nothing is written outside it.\n\nPick it in the next screen — use its New folder button if it does not exist yet.
That folder is outside the vault (%1$s). Pick one inside it.
Pick a folder inside the vault, not the vault root itself.
Nothing chosen — tick at least one
Regenerates an index note for every included folder, plus one at the top linking them together. Existing maps are backed up first.\n\nBackups kept per map:
In the Pebble app: Settings → Index → Webhooks. Set the trigger to double-click-hold, paste the URL, and add a header with the name and value below.
Generating a new secret stops the current one working until you paste the new one into the Pebble app.
Folder is a single name under %1$s — “%2$s” was shortened to “%3$s”.
That folder is outside %1$s. Rules can only write inside it.
Replaces every routing rule with the bundled defaults and writes them to the vault. The old config file is backed up first. Notes already filed are not touched.
%1$s. Those names were old defaults rather than choices, so they have been updated. Anything already filed stays where it is — move it across when convenient.
Config file is from an older version
%1$s was written before the folder change, so it was not loaded — its folder names meant something different. The bundled defaults are in use; set your rules up again and the file is rewritten.
No rules yet. Reload from the vault or add one.
Give the rule at least one keyword
“%1$s” is already used by another rule

The words that make this rule fire. Enter several separated by commas — “blog idea, blog post idea, content idea” is one rule with three ways of saying the same thing.

Spaces inside a phrase are fine; only commas separate.

Matching is on whole words, so “task” does not fire on “multitasking”. Case and punctuation are ignored.

What happens when the rule fires, and which of the fields below apply at all.

File writes a note into a folder. Task writes a task file into the task folder. Timer starts a timer in the clock app. Calendar opens a new event.

Timer and Calendar write nothing to the vault, so they have no folder or tags.

A single folder name, created inside the app\'s base folder — not a path elsewhere in the vault. The app only ever writes inside its own folder.\n\nFor Task rules this is fixed: every task goes to the task folder.

Written into the note\'s frontmatter, not as inline hashtags, so Dataview and Metadata Menu can read them.\n\nOn a Task rule these override the default task tags, so a “work task” route and a “home task” route can carry different ones. Leave them as shown to inherit the default.
Which rule wins when one recording matches more than one. Lower runs first, and the first match is the one that fires.\n\nIf no recording ever matches two of your rules, this never matters.
Switch a rule off to take it out of matching without deleting it. Recordings it would have caught fall through to the rules below, and then to the default route.
Notes are filed into the folder, tagged in frontmatter.
Each task is written as its own file in the task folder. Folder and tags come from settings, so they are not set per rule.
Fires a timer at the clock app. Nothing is written to the vault, so folder and tags do not apply.
Opens a calendar event. Nothing is written to the vault, so folder and tags do not apply.
Where a recording goes when no rule matches. It always runs, so there is no keyword or priority to set.
That folder is outside the vault (%1$s). Choose one inside it.
Set the vault root first, under Vault access.
That one wrote no file — a timer or calendar entry has nothing to move.
No file access yet. On GrapheneOS use Storage Scopes — see File access below.

On GrapheneOS, use Storage Scopes: App info → Permissions → Storage → Storage Scopes, then add the folders listed under Vault access.

Do not grant “All files access” — Storage Scopes is only offered while the app holds no storage permission, so granting it removes the option.

On stock Android there is no Storage Scopes, and All files access is the only way to reach the vault by path.
The rule is saved, but “%1$s” is not in this app\'s Storage Scopes, so notes routed there cannot be written. Add it, then the rule works.
That is a folder inside the vault

You granted “%1$s”, but the app writes to paths that start with “%1$s/” — so notes would land in %1$s/%1$s/. It also cannot see %2$s from there, so tasks could not reach your daily note.\n\nGrant the vault root instead. If you meant to grant only this folder, the paths can be adjusted to suit — but only file and audio routes will work.
Cannot see the rest of the vault
This folder has no “%1$s” in it, so tasks cannot reach your daily note and file routes cannot reach their folders. Grant the vault root — the folder that contains %1$s.
Paths adjusted: notes and audio now go directly inside %1$s
Vault grant looks wrong — tap “Grant vault folder”
Fires when a recording is routed as %1$s. Pick its sound here.
Fires when a recording matched no rule and was filed to the inbox.
Each step of handling a webhook, for working out why one did not do what was expected. Verbose.
No file written for this route.
No rule matched — going to the inbox

Tick a route to be told when it fires. Each has its own notification channel, so its sound is chosen in Android\'s notification settings for this app — not here.\n\nFailures always notify and are not listed: a recording that went nowhere must never pass quietly.
Inherited from the task tags setting until you set your own.
Granted as a folder tree (not a plain path)
A single folder name, created under the base folder. Anything already filed stays where it is — renaming here does not move it.
How deeply the inbox and recordings are filed by date. Both take a file per recording and never lose one, so left flat they become unusable to browse.
Comma separated. Written on every task unless a rule sets its own. #task is load-bearing: the daily note\'s queries filter on it.
Every pipeline milestone as a notification. Verbose.
Each route has its own channel — pick its sound in Android\'s settings
The loopback port the receiver binds. Changing it means changing the URL in the Pebble app too.
Port changed — stop and start the receiver, and update the Pebble app\'s URL.
How many timestamped copies of each map to keep before the oldest is pruned.
Read the vault file and replace the rules held here
Write what is held here back to the vault file
Discard the rules and start from the bundled defaults
Nothing on the dictation route yet. Say your dictation keyword first — other routes are deliberately not offered here.
The last dictation was %1$s ago, past the %2$d minute cutoff. Dictate again, or raise the cutoff in settings.

Tapping the mic key on your keyboard commits the ring\'s most recent transcription instead of listening. It has to be enabled once as an input method in Android\'s settings; it is never the system recogniser, so ordinary voice typing is untouched.
How old the last dictation may be and still be committed. Without a cutoff, tapping the mic key hours later commits that morning\'s words into whatever field is focused.
How many recent transcriptions the keyboard can reach. The newest is the one committed.
✓ The mic key will reach this.
✗ Not enabled as an input method yet — the mic key cannot reach it.
✗ Enabled, but the system is not listing it as a voice input method, so the mic key cannot reach it.
✗ “%1$s” is ahead of this in the system\'s voice list, and the keyboard takes the first. Disable it to use the ring instead.
No keywords yet — this rule cannot fire. Expand it to add one.
Whole word anywhere in the transcript
Only at the start of the transcript
How a keyword is compared against what was said. Whole word is the default and the only one that behaves sanely on speech: matching anywhere inside another word fires “task” inside “multitasking”.
Whether this rule\'s folder gets its own Map of Content note when you rebuild the map tree, and is linked from the top-level index. Turn it off for a folder nobody browses through an index.

Fires when a %1$s route needs a tap because Android blocked the app from starting it directly. This one is how the action actually happens, so it is always on — grant \"Display over other apps\" to stop needing the tap.
A new event carries only a title, so it lands in the next free slot. Sending the phrase to an app that parses language gets the date and time out of what was said.

A new event is standard and any calendar app can take it, but it carries no date or time. Sending the phrase hands the whole thing to one named app, whose own parser reads \"tomorrow at noon\" — at the cost of naming that app.
Send the phrase to one app to parse
App to send the phrase to

The package name of the app whose parser reads the phrase. Named rather than chosen from a list on purpose: sharing plain text is offered by every messaging app, and a share sheet in front of a private voice note is one tap from sending it to a contact.
✓ Installed — the phrase goes straight there, with no chooser.
✗ Not installed — the route falls back to a plain new event.
(content hidden — turn on detailed content logging to see it here)

What was said is kept in the routing log so a recording can be traced, and the log is the only place a dictation\'s words exist at all. These decide how long that lasts and whether notifications repeat it.

Hours. Anything older is removed and a dated marker is left in its place. Zero keeps the log until you clear it, which is a diagnostic setting rather than an everyday one.\n\nThis does not touch your notes, tasks or recordings in the vault — those are meant to be there. A dictation writes nothing else, so this is the only control over it.
Let notifications repeat what was said. Off by default — a notification carrying the words puts them on the lock screen.

Everything in the log goes, and a dated marker is left in its place. Your notes, tasks and recordings in the vault are untouched.\n\nA dictation waiting for the keyboard is held here and nowhere else, so clearing now means the mic key has nothing to offer.
Only when it opens the phrase

Takes the word that fired this rule out of what gets written or handed on, so \"task call Fred\" becomes \"call Fred\".\n\nIt is only ever removed from the **start** of what was said. A keyword used mid-sentence is left alone — \"remind me about the task tomorrow\" keeps its words — so turning this on cannot eat the middle of a sentence.
